entity.name: Samuel Appiah Kubi
entity.description: Open-source Python framework unifying satellite data access across 22 verified providers, featuring a physics-based InSAR chain, optical pixel offset tracking, and automatic multi-modal fallback for deformation monitoring.
entity.sustainability: After the funding period, pygeofetch will continue to be maintained through community contributions, academic partnerships, and potential commercial support for custom deployments. The core tool will remain MIT-licensed and open.

projects.name: pygeofetch
projects.description:
A federated open-source geospatial data pipeline unifying search and download across 22 satellite data providers. Includes a physics-based InSAR processing chain (burst-synchronization preflight, orbit-based coregistration, SBAS time series, Cramer-Rao uncertainty quantification) and optical pixel offset tracking for deformation monitoring where InSAR structurally fails (e.g. large-magnitude mining subsidence, co-seismic displacement).

Validation: a full, real, published-literature-referenced InSAR run at Mexico City (cross-checked qualitatively against Cigna & Tapete 2021's documented subsidence pattern); a second case study at Bu'ertai Mine (Shendong Coalfield), a site published literature confirms defeats conventional InSAR, where the pipeline automatically detected InSAR's real coverage collapse and handed off to optical offset tracking without manual intervention.

Adoption: early-stage — see real, current GitHub metrics on the repository. Users include researchers in Ghana and Nigeria.

plans.name: Automated Testing & Validation
plans.description: Maintaining regression test suites (sub-pixel optical offset accuracy, InSAR phase-unwrapping correctness, strain outlier capping) and the cloud compute needed to run them against real Sentinel-1/2 data.
plans.justification: Covers cloud compute costs for real, periodic Sentinel-1/2 regression tests.

plans.name: Community Support
plans.description: Time allocated for issue triage, PR reviews, and lowering the barrier to entry for new researchers and engineers.
plans.justification: Covers dedicated hours for issue triage, PR review, and contributor onboarding.

plans.name: Cloud Compute & CI/CD
plans.description: Infrastructure to automatically test processing pipelines on every commit, ensuring new code does not break real geospatial workflows.
plans.justification: Covers CI minutes for real, automated test runs against representative-sized data.

plans.name: Educational Content & Case Studies
plans.description: Production of real, fully-reproducible tutorial notebooks (e.g. the Mexico City and Bu'ertai case studies) for the official documentation, each cross-checked against source code and published literature before publication.
plans.justification: Covers approximately 40 hours at $100/hr to produce two reproducible case studies.
